items.title: Define the private paid consultation workflow
acceptance: Use a free discovery call before issuing a private paid Foundation invitation in the client language.

Release definitive unpaid expiry. Route late payments to review; require signed operator preview and confirmation for replacement bookings after checking availability. Never request wallet secrets.

Commercial terms remain tracked in CC-29.

Test BLIK and card success, cancellation, failure, refunds and receipt reconciliation.

items.title: Add discount codes to Foundation bookings across PLN and BTC
acceptance: Add an optional, collapsed Have a discount code? / Masz kod rabatowy? control before checkout creation. Apply or remove a code without creating a Cal booking. Show the original PLN price, discount and final total in the selected language; changing between PLN and BTC preserves the applied code.

Use one server-owned code catalogue for both payment methods. Support percentage or fixed-PLN discounts, activation and expiry timestamps, disabling, Foundation-only eligibility and global usage limits. Normalize codes consistently, allow one code per booking and reject stacking, 100% discounts or totals below the configured positive checkout minimum. Keep referral schemes, bundles and customer segmentation out of the first version.

Calculate amounts on the server using integer grosz and a documented percentage-rounding rule. Never trust a submitted discount or total. Persist an immutable booking price snapshot: original amount, code ID/version, discount, net PLN amount and currency before creating a payment request.

Charge the same discounted PLN value through Stripe or use it as the fiat price for the BTCPay invoice, which quotes the BTC amount at invoice creation. For example, 10% off 420 PLN produces a 42 PLN discount and a 378 PLN invoice on either rail. Do not apply a second provider-side discount or attempt to reuse the original BTC quote after expiry.

Replace the fixed 420 PLN settlement assumption with verification against each booking's persisted net price and linked provider invoice/session. Verify the expected currency and settlement rules for each rail. Keep verified, signed and idempotent settlement as the prerequisite for Cal confirmation; show the stored discount and total on the confirmation page and in appropriate receipts.

Reserve limited-use code capacity atomically with the payment attempt and consume it once on eligible settlement. Release unpaid reservations on definitive checkout expiry or cancellation. Duplicate submissions, webhook retries, provider switching and concurrent customers must not exceed the limit or redeem the code twice. A late payment after release requires reconciliation rather than automatic redemption or confirmation.

Freeze the price once checkout exists. Reject code changes on an active invoice/session; any replacement flow must first invalidate the old payment request and preserve one booking and one redemption. Refund calculations use the actual discounted amount paid. Obtain the owner's policy for whether cancellation or refund restores a code before implementing automatic restoration.

Provide a restricted operator command or existing admin mechanism to create, disable and inspect codes and usage without exposing credentials. Record code changes and redemptions for reconciliation. Rate-limit validation attempts and do not send submitted customer details to public logs.

Verify valid, unknown, expired, disabled, ineligible and exhausted codes; both discount types and rounding; invalid client totals; concurrent final-use attempts; abandoned checkout and slot expiry; provider switching; duplicate or late settlement; and refunds. Test EN/PL display and real discounted Stripe sandbox plus BTCPay test-network settlement before a live pilot.
items.notes: Future enhancement scoped on November 5, 2026; no discount UI, code catalogue or payment behavior is implemented by this item. Implement after the baseline paid booking flow passes CC-33. Prefer a shared application-level price calculation over Stripe-only promotion codes so PLN and BTC have matching eligibility, usage limits and pricing. Owner decisions before implementation: campaign values, eligibility dates and limits, minimum payable total, and restoration policy after refunds or cancellation.

items.title: Persist booking price, currency and payment rail before production
acceptance: Store an immutable server-calculated amount/currency/version snapshot before checkout. Approved initial catalogue: PLN 420, EUR 95, GBP 80; new BTC bookings receive 10% off the PLN base. Existing checkouts keep their agreed price.
Validate both provider settlement and manual late-payment resolution against the stored snapshot; remove global fixed-price assumptions from creation, recovery, result UI and refunds.

Separate language, price currency, provider and rail (card/BLIK, Bitcoin on-chain, Lightning). Preserve existing client contracts through an explicit compatibility mapping; currency is not a payment method.

Migrate existing bookings conservatively with the known legacy 420 PLN price; retain payment IDs, tokens and provider associations. Test migration, tampered totals, switching, late settlement and duplicate notifications.
items.notes: Stored immutable amount/currency/version snapshots now drive checkout creation, BTC recovery, automatic settlement, late-payment resolution and result display. Legacy records retain 420 PLN; approved EUR/GBP catalogue and 10% new-BTC pricing deployed/tested. Owner reports card-to-BTC discount passed. A fully explicit rail model and complete historical migration/refund acceptance remain to verify before closure.

items.title: Make production configuration explicit and verify recovery
acceptance: Centralize validated public site/API/return origins, environment and Bitcoin network; eliminate hard-coded staging URLs and integration identifiers from the production path. Reject mismatched live/test configurations.
Isolate production and staging credentials, databases, stores and webhooks. Verify supported Node runtime on build host and VPS, backup restoration and rollback without losing paid-booking records.

Add bounded provider reconciliation for pending payments and unresolved late-payment cases after missed webhooks or restarts; reuse verified, idempotent decisions and never reclaim a released slot automatically.
Expose actionable operator failures for payment verified but Cal confirmation failed; exercise retry/recovery and establish an operator review procedure.
Complete remaining CC-33 scenarios and owner-approved low-value live pilot, including refund and webhook-outage recovery, before enabling real client invitations.
items.notes: Environment-specific origin, Stripe mode, BTCPay identity and production database guards deployed to staging. Node 24 deployment preflight passed without old engine warnings. On 2026-11-07 owner reported Events-read preflight, SQLite backup/isolated restore, running BTC/Stripe recovery flags and HTTP400 unsigned-webhook check passed. Recovery is enabled; controlled missed-webhook tests are still pending. Production provisioning, runtime verification, off-server backup drill, operator retry evidence and live pilot remain open.

Prefer BTCPay as invoice authority if the plugin passes; document direct Blink adapter only as fallback, including authenticated callbacks, provider re-read, payment-hash correlation and recovery after missed events.

Record custody choice, fees, limits, liquidity/service availability, balance monitoring, withdrawal procedure and refund ownership. Choose BTC settlement explicitly; do not silently select Stablesats.
Document actual Lightning expiry and on-chain/LN concurrent-payment behavior before deciding how methods can coexist. No live activation as part of this investigation.

Persist invoice and Lightning payment-hash association; verify amount, currency, reference and settled state server-side before confirming Cal exactly once.
Show Lightning waiting/paid states and payment reference without blockchain confirmations, block height or mining loader. Preserve on-chain confirmation UI.

Test expiry, payment at expiry, duplicate and out-of-order events, missing webhooks, restart, provider outage, invoice regeneration and both rails paid. Extra or late payments enter review; released slots require explicit resolution.
Run staging-compatible tests and a separately approved limited live pilot; provide disable and recovery procedures.
items.notes: Planned 2026-11-06. See docs/PAYMENT-EXPANSION.md. Planning only; not implemented or deployed.

items.title: Approve multi-currency pricing and enable PLN EUR CHF GBP USD
acceptance: Use owner-approved fixed ratios derived from one editable PLN/EUR/GBP anchor. Initial prices are PLN 420, EUR 95 and GBP 80. Obtain explicit prices before enabling CHF or USD charge currencies; USD payment equivalents are informational.
Let clients select charge currency independently from language and payment rail before checkout. Show the final charge currency and total clearly; disable currencies without approved prices.
Freeze price/currency once a payment request exists; replacement requires safe invalidation or review of the existing request. Preserve booking identity and prevent two payable checkouts.

Validate merchant-specific Stripe currency/method support, BTCPay rates and settlement/accounting needs. Offer BLIK only for eligible PLN checkouts; do not treat display conversion as a different charge currency.

Test each enabled currency across eligible rails, formatting, rounding, refunds, receipts, tampering and late reconciliation. Extend CC-38 discounts using the same pricing snapshot rather than a second price engine.
items.notes: PLN 420, EUR 95 and GBP 80 approved, implemented and owner-tested on staging. One configurable anchor updates all approved fixed ratios; currency selection is a compact BTC/PLN/EUR/GBP row. BTC sats estimate and small USD equivalent are display-only; USD and CHF charge currencies remain disabled and unpriced. Multi-currency refund and additional rail acceptance remain open.
